title: How wine is sold
subtitle: From vineyard to glass
objectives: Describe the route from producer to consumer

steps.title: The chain
steps.body: A bottle passes through several hands. The producer sells to an importer or distributor, who sells to retailers and restaurants, who sell to you. Each step adds a margin. Large producers may also sell directly through cellar doors, clubs and online, keeping more of the price.

steps.title: Three tiers
steps.body: In the United States, a law from 1933, after Prohibition, created the three-tier system: producers must sell to wholesalers, who sell to retailers or restaurants. Each state sets its own rules, and some sell alcohol only through state-run shops. In many other markets, importers and distributors play similar roles, but with fewer legal restrictions.

steps.prompt: What does the US three-tier system require?
options: Producers sell to wholesalers, who sell to retailers
Only state shops may sell wine
steps.explanation: The system separates producers, wholesalers and retailers, though some states allow exceptions.

steps.title: Channels
steps.body: Off-trade means shops and supermarkets, where most wine is sold. On-trade means restaurants and bars, with higher margins. Direct to consumer includes cellar doors, wine clubs and online sales. Supermarkets dominate volume in the UK and much of Europe; on-trade shapes a wine's image.

steps.prompt: Match each channel to its description.
steps.explanation: Each channel has different margins and roles.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Wine moves from producer through importers and retailers
The US uses a legal three-tier system
Off-trade, on-trade and direct sales are the main channels
